newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil firms, jet slips.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil firms, jet slips.

text.p: Singapore diesel prices rose on Monday as a local trader extended his recent buying spree for the third week running but jet fuel fell as the same trader withdrew from the market.
Traders said apart from the Singapore's intent to buy more physical cargoes, the market is also supported by a belief that the Chinese are expected to come in and buy in a big way.
Low stocks in Hong Kong which had in recent weeks enjoyed booming barge sales to south China has led to enquiries there for replenishment cargoes.
Traders said Hong Kong is expected to seek about 200,000-tonnes in the coming days to cover for its low stocks.

But terminal operators there are holding back their purchases in the hope that prices will come off once the anticipated arbitrage cargoes of about 500,000 barrels begin to arrive sometime in early April.
In the Singapore physical market, the local trader, who had for the past two weeks to Friday bought a total of 2.32 million, was bidding for a April 6-10 cargo at $27.60 per barrel.
And a Japanese trader was bidding for an April 1-5 cargo at $28.50 per barrel, free-on-board (fob) Singapore.
There were no offers for product lifting in early April. The offers from traders and a major were for cargoes loading from April 11 onwards at $27.50, $27.60 and $27.90 per barrel, respectively.
Sources said some of the cargoes offered were part the arbitrage cargoes that is headed to this region from the West.
Rising physical prices also led to firmer swap prices where April traded to a high of $26.15 per barrel. April swaps were last quoted at $25.80/$26.00 up from Friday's $25.40/$25.60.
As with last year, Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has declined to accept all offers for its one-year term diesel and kerosene tenders.
Sources said IOC is expected to re-issue the tenders shortly.
Jet fuel prices fell after the local trader who had over the same two week period bought 1.4 million barrels withdrew from the market.
A trader was offering a 100,000-barrel cargo at $27.60 per barrel fob but no bids were seen against it.
